title: Analytic: vertical dipole between parallel PEC plates, TM1 cutoff kink (3D FDTD)
description:
A z-oriented electric point dipole (current moment Il = 1e-12 A m, gaussian pulse at 1.33 um, bandwidth 0.5) between two perfectly conducting plates (em_fdtd_3d, 25 nm cells): bc_z_lo / bc_z_hi pec plus a pec_domain on the next cell layer of each, so each conductor is two cells thick and its surface (the pinned tangential E) lies at the centre of its inner layer: z = 1.5 dx and L_z - 1.5 dx, gap d = 30 dx = 0.75 um. CPML (16 cells) on the four side faces, the plates running into them. The dipole sits on the E_z face at z = 9 dx, z0 = 7.5 dx = d/4 above the lower surface. A flux box with its bottom and top faces inside the conductors (between their two layers: zero flux) and its side faces at 0.2 / 1.0 um collects the power guided away between the plates.
Analytic (mode sum: TEM plus the TM_n modes whose cutoff 2d/n lies above lambda; only n = 1 in this band): P / P0 = (3 lambda / (4 d)) [1 + 2 sum_n (1 - (n lambda / (2 d))^2) cos^2(n pi z0 / d)], P0 = eta0 k^2 (Il)^2 / (12 pi) of the free dipole; 1.556 at 1 um, 1.632 at 1.25 um, 1.5 at the TM1 cutoff 2 d = 1.5 um (slope -1 below, +1 above: a kink), 1.8 at 1.8 um (TEM only, 3 lambda / (4 d)).
Derived values tab: P_ratio_1000, P_ratio_1250, P_ratio_1800 (power_per_cw / P0 at 1.0, 1.25, 1.8 um) with the references.
Curves & tables tab: P_over_P0 (the flux box power_per_cw over P0(lambda)) with the dotted mode-sum reference: the kink at 1.5 um.
Spectra tab: em.radiated_power quantity power_per_cw vs the dashed P0(lambda) P / P0 (no sample on the cutoff itself; the samples next to it, 1.487 / 1.513 um, ring longest).
Expected agreement: ~0.5 % away from the cutoff (lattice dispersion and box quadrature as dipole_over_pec_ground_3d, the discrete TM1 cutoff ~5e-4 longer, CPML reflection of the guided waves); worse within ~2 % of the cutoff, where the TM1 group velocity goes to 0 (slow transit, weak CPML absorption, a long ring-down within the 300 fs run); to be confirmed by a first run.
